description: External RabbitMQ configuration inconsistencies in the spring-cloud-dataflow chart: no secret-key parameter, a hardcoded secret key in the consumers, and bundled-subchart password validation applied to the external path
_fidelity: Rebuilt from source at the pinned SHA. The previous key attributed drift points 2 and 3 (rabbitmq.auth.password / rabbitmq.auth.erlangCookie validation) to templates/_helpers.tpl. That file contains NEITHER string — both live in templates/NOTES.txt:86-87, which the old key never mentioned and which task.toml still demotes to sufficient_files. Its override_chains also cited 'values.yaml: rabbitmq.auth.erlangCookie' and 'values.yaml: rabbitmq.auth.password'; erlangCookie occurs 0 times in values.yaml. Drift point 1's core claim was real but its mechanism was wrong: scdf.rabbitmq.secretName (_helpers.tpl:338-346) resolves only a NAME and never reads a key, so the fixed-key assumption is not there — it is hardcoded in the consumers (externalrabbitmq-secrets.yaml:18, skipper/configmap.yaml:52). The key also undercounted: PR #24493 changes 5 template/values files, not 3. expected_solution.json separately demanded a field named existingPasswordSecretPasswordKey, which occurs 0 times in the real chart (the PR adds externalRabbitmq.existingSecret + existingSecretPasswordKey).

scenario.values: rabbitmq.enabled=false, externalRabbitmq.enabled=true, externalRabbitmq.password set inline (externalRabbitmq.existingPasswordSecret unset)
scenario.note: The NOTES.txt validation is gated by `or (rabbitmq.enabled) (and (externalRabbitmq.enabled) (not externalRabbitmq.existingPasswordSecret))` at NOTES.txt:85. With an existing secret supplied the block is SKIPPED, so the drift only manifests on the inline-password path. instruction.md was corrected to match; it previously claimed the demand persists 'even when we have provided our own secret', which the guard contradicts.

drift_points.expected: a secret NAME plus a configurable KEY, mirroring the external-database pattern (externalDatabase.existingPasswordSecret at :1881 paired with externalDatabase.existingPasswordKey at :1884)
drift_points.actual: name only — there is no externalRabbitmq key parameter at all, so the key the secret stores the password under cannot be expressed
drift_points.override_chain: values.yaml:externalRabbitmq.existingPasswordSecret -> _helpers.tpl:scdf.rabbitmq.secretName (resolves the NAME only) -> consumers hardcode the key

drift_points.expected: read the password from the key named by a configurable parameter
drift_points.actual: - SPRING_RABBITMQ_PASSWORD=${rabbitmq-password} — the key 'rabbitmq-password' is hardcoded, so an existing secret must happen to use exactly that key. externalrabbitmq-secrets.yaml:18 hardcodes the same key when generating the secret

drift_points.expected: not required on the external path — an Erlang cookie is a bundled-subchart clustering concern and is meaningless for an external broker. PR #24493 gates the block on .Values.rabbitmq.enabled
drift_points.actual: $requiredErlangPassword := dict "valueKey" "rabbitmq.auth.erlangCookie" ... — validated whenever externalRabbitmq.enabled and no existingPasswordSecret, so rendering fails until an irrelevant value is supplied

drift_points.expected: include "scdf.rabbitmq.secretName" . — the helper that honours externalRabbitmq.existingPasswordSecret
drift_points.actual: include "scdf.rabbitmq.fullname" . — always names the BUNDLED subchart's secret, so validation errors point external users at a secret that does not exist in their deployment
drift_points.override_chain: NOTES.txt:77 $secretNameRabbitmq -> scdf.rabbitmq.fullname -> error message names the wrong secret

not_drifted.note: Named by the OLD key for the rabbitmq.auth.password and erlangCookie validation. It contains NEITHER string (0 fixed-string hits each). scdf.rabbitmq.secretName at :338-346 is a name resolver and is essentially correct; PR #24493 touches it only to extend it. instruction.md names this file, so citing it is prompt-following, not evidence.

scoring_evidence._comment: Tokens absent from instruction.md, verified with fixed-string grep -coF. The prompt SUPPLIES 'rabbitmq.auth.erlangCookie' (1), 'rabbitmq.auth.password' (1), '_helpers.tpl' (1), 'externalrabbitmq-secrets.yaml' (1) and 'skipper/configmap.yaml' (1) — none may be graded. It never names NOTES.txt, where the validation actually lives, nor the secret KEY names, nor the external-database precedent field. Note the fixed-string discipline matters here: 'rabbitmq.auth.erlangCookie' leaks but the secret field 'rabbitmq-erlang-cookie' does not, and a regex '.' would conflate the two.

verification.method: gh_api_pr_files + raw source at pinned SHA
verification.verified_at_sha: PR #24493 changes 7 files; 5 are template/values (NOTES.txt, _helpers.tpl, externalrabbitmq-secrets.yaml, skipper/configmap.yaml, values.yaml) plus Chart.yaml and README.md. Confirmed at 53aca511: _helpers.tpl contains 0 hits for 'auth.password' and 'erlangCookie'; NOTES.txt:86-87 contains both; values.yaml contains 0 hits for 'erlangCookie'; externalDatabase pairs existingPasswordSecret (:1881) with existingPasswordKey (:1884) while externalRabbitmq has only existingPasswordSecret (:1975); externalrabbitmq-secrets.yaml:18 and skipper/configmap.yaml:52 both hardcode the key 'rabbitmq-password'; NOTES.txt:77 uses scdf.rabbitmq.fullname. Chart.yaml at the SHA is version 26.11.0 and the PR bumps to 26.12.0, so the pinned tree is pre-fix.
